chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Musanna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the man who performs Tawaf without being in ablution. Can he count that Tawaf? He said: No.
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir, establishes the invalidity of Tawaf performed without Wudu, distinguishing it from the majority opinion that only Khufah (minor impurity) is required. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on ritual purity as a prerequisite for the validity of specific acts of worship, reflecting the rigorous standards of the Ahl al-Bayt's jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Musna, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the man who performs Tawaaf without being in ablution. Can he count that as the Tawaaf?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muthanna’ from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Tawaf without wudu’; if such Tawaf is counted.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not counted.’”
